findings.burn: Moving the burn aft is the lever: every geometry with the burn 4 m or more aft gives 0.73-1.04 MN, median 0.96 MN (four engines), against 0.44 MN as drawn. The closure factor (x3 to x6), grading and aft spacing mostly stay within the sampling error (+-6 points of debris hit share at 24 directions, about +-0.1 MN); none is a clear win over x4 at 4 m.
findings.closure: Stronger closure coils matter mainly through the capture current: with the burn 4 m aft the field that stops the pulse needs 286 GJ per engine instead of 3090 GJ as drawn, still 26x the 11 GJ the drawn coils carry.
findings.cavity: Plasma picture: letting the debris expand as an unmagnetised bubble to R_b = 1.5 m before the field acts changes the research result by -3 % in thrust; as drawn the bubble (0.6 m) reaches nothing. Both pictures bracket a coupled plasma (still not modelled).
findings.pickup: Re-tracing the X-ray and neutron pickup for the moved burn: the hardware covers 40 % of the sky instead of 72 %, so the design-target heat falls from 2,188x to 1,155x the radiator share (ENG-065 had kept the old pickup and reported 1,967x).
findings.balance: Momentum balance (D debris, units of one particle momentum): as drawn the ship gets 0.33, made of +0.65 from particles striking the shield and closure hardware and -0.32 through the field: a pusher plate, not a nozzle. With the burn 4 m aft the ship gets 0.79, +0.68 through the field and +0.10 by impact. Closure 0e+00.
findings.combination: Combined, not multiplied: research geometry plus 80 % early extraction gives 0.36 MN at 228x; multiplying the separate gains would claim 0.94 MN at 256x. Extraction moves energy into fast products that carry almost no momentum, so it removes the thrust the topology won; the two levers compete.
findings.hydrogen: Hydrogen reaction mass: inelastic mixing keeps the impulse and lowers the exhaust speed; only ideal elastic transfer (no physics yet) raises thrust, x3.81 with ten times the debris mass. Coupling OPEN.
findings.coils: Coils at the capture current, burn 4 m aft: 286 GJ per engine, 30 T at the windings (above the 20-25 T REBCO practice), 16.1 GN axial on one coil, a 19 min dump at 50 kA and 10 kV, or 3,579 t of copper to absorb it. The drawn research geometry (closure x4 at the as-built current) carries 27 GJ, 12.5 T, 41 t of hoop structure; it does not capture the pulse.
findings.frontier: Lowest heat anywhere: Early extraction: 80% of the product energy leaves the target (mirror4|5) 0.39 MN at 165x, Early extraction: 80% of the product energy leaves the target (mirror6|6) 0.40 MN at 170x
findings.none: No geometry, lever or combination closes: the lowest heat found is 164x the radiator share, and thrust stays near a twentieth of the 21.8 MN need.
